svg.title: Risk Model Training & Eval
svg.desc: Proposed internal ML architecture for the Enterprise AI Agent Sales and Risk System. This static drill-down matches the Agent Evaluation and Observability diagram; interactive navigation is not implemented. Feature and Dataset Preparation starts from governed, validated CRM and project data in Snowflake, reusing the analytics team's established computation framework. S3 retains original source inputs; Snowflake holds prepared business data and features. dbt runs feature engineering on Snowflake compute. Features include committed versus available capacity, schedule slack, product mix, bottleneck load and historical yield variability, calculated using only information available at the prediction timestamp. Versioned feature and label snapshots retain customer, project, prediction date, source version, feature-definition version and label-definition version. Labels derive from observed delivery outcomes relative to an explicitly versioned promise date, not from unreviewed LLM opinions. Outcome maturity is checked; incomplete projects are not labeled successful by default. Temporal Split separates train, validation and final holdout windows, with project grouping and any necessary purge gap to prevent overlapping outcomes or repeated project records from leaking future information across splits. Transformations requiring learned statistics are fitted only on training data. Hyperparameters and risk thresholds are chosen on validation data. The final holdout is reserved for final assessment, not repeatedly used for tuning. Apache Airflow orchestrates this model-update workload. It is separate from daily batch scoring; retraining is not required for every daily scoring run. Versioned training snapshots are exported to S3 only for model-update jobs. AWS SageMaker executes training jobs. MLflow logs parameters, dataset references, code versions, metrics and run identifiers; trained model and preprocessing artifacts are stored in S3 with immutable references. Model Evaluation runs reproducible metric calculations and deterministic assertions with pytest; MLflow stores evaluation results. Precision, recall and PR-AUC assess delivery-risk classification. Recall is compared at a documented operating threshold and review workload, together with precision and alert volume. Calibration and alert lead time are assessed using explicit definitions, including false early alerts. Critical business slices cover customers, products, plants and risk levels. Version Comparison evaluates candidate and current baseline on the same frozen holdout and operating policy, with uncertainty and slice regressions considered. Baseline-versus-candidate metrics are not claims of measured project results. The Model Promotion Gate implements acceptance policies and protected delivery checks in GitHub Actions; MLflow is not a standalone deployment authorization service. A failed gate returns the candidate for revision. Changes informed by holdout results require a fresh reserved evaluation period before release; the return loop does not authorize tuning on the same holdout. Only a passing candidate is registered and selected for serving in this simplified workflow. A registry may also retain unapproved versions in a full implementation; registration alone does not grant production approval. Snowflake Model Registry holds approved production deployment versions controlled by the same promotion workflow. MLflow retains experiment and evaluation records, linked by run ID and immutable artifact digest. Candidate compatibility checks verify input signatures, fitted preprocessing dependencies and prediction parity in an isolated Snowflake environment before production promotion. A SageMaker container or archive is not assumed to be directly deployable unchanged. Batch Risk Scoring resolves the approved version once and pins its immutable model and feature snapshot for the job. Snowflake warehouse inference scores validated daily features and publishes checked scores in Snowflake. Daily scoring does not export feature batches or results to SageMaker. The diagram shows model selection, not all inference-data inputs. Its scores feed the risk dashboards and scoped Agent Context shown in the system overview. Postdeployment drift and delayed-label quality monitoring remain in shared governance. Security, auditing, artifact encryption and rollback controls are shared capabilities abstracted from this module view. All labels are English and logos retain native colors in consistent 32-pixel frames. No business performance is asserted.
svg.text: Enterprise AI Agent Sales & Risk System
